dq-0129.question: According to the table, how much did the mean light intensity needed for detection decrease from 0 minutes to 20 minutes?
dq-0129.explanation: Correct: B. The mean fell from 50 to 10, a decrease of 40 units.

distractor_notes.A: 10 is the mean intensity at 20 minutes, not the decrease.
distractor_notes.C: 50 is the mean intensity at 0 minutes, not the decrease.
distractor_notes.D: 60 comes from adding the two values instead of subtracting.

dq-0130.question: The light intensity measured in this study is an example of which of the following?
dq-0130.explanation: Correct: D. Detecting a stimulus half of the time defines the absolute threshold.

distractor_notes.A: A just-noticeable difference is the smallest detectable change between two stimuli.
distractor_notes.B: Sensory interaction is senses influencing each other.
distractor_notes.C: Transduction converts stimuli into neural messages.

dq-0131.question: Dr. Moreno randomly assigns 60 volunteers to take either melatonin or a placebo one hour before bed. She then measures how long it takes each volunteer to fall asleep. Which of the following is the control group in this study?
options: The group that took the placebo
The group that fell asleep first
dq-0131.explanation: Correct: B. The control group receives no real treatment and serves as the comparison, here the placebo group.

distractor_notes.A: This group receives the treatment being tested.
distractor_notes.C: Falling asleep first is a result, not a group assigned in advance.
distractor_notes.D: A control group is a comparison group, not the whole sample.

dq-0132.question: A researcher measures activity in the amygdala of 40 participants using fMRI while they view photographs. She then compares each participant's activity with the participant's score on an anxiety questionnaire. Which of the following research designs is the researcher using?
dq-0132.explanation: Correct: C. The researcher measures two variables and compares them without manipulating either, which is correlational.

distractor_notes.A: No variable is manipulated and no one is assigned to conditions.
distractor_notes.B: A case study examines one individual or a small group in depth.
distractor_notes.D: Participants are viewing photographs in a lab, not being observed in a natural setting.

dq-0133.question: Dr. Idowu studies one patient who lost the ability to form new memories after brain surgery and reports the findings in detail. Which of the following is the most important limitation of this research design?
options: Results from one person may not apply to others.
Case studies cannot describe behavior in much detail.
Case studies always break ethical guidelines for research.
Case studies cannot be used to study the human brain.
dq-0133.explanation: Correct: A. Results from a single case may not generalize to the wider population.

distractor_notes.B: Case studies are known for rich detail.
distractor_notes.C: Case studies can follow ethical guidelines.
distractor_notes.D: Case studies are often used to study brain damage.

dq-0134.question: A researcher testing a new sleep medication gives volunteers pills without telling them about the possible side effects. Which of the following ethical guidelines was most clearly violated?
dq-0134.explanation: Correct: D. Participants must be told about risks beforehand so they can agree knowingly, which is informed consent.

distractor_notes.A: Debriefing is explaining the study after it ends.
distractor_notes.B: Confidentiality is keeping data private.
distractor_notes.C: The stem does not say participants were prevented from leaving.

dq-0135.question: Seven participants spent the following numbers of minutes in REM sleep during one night: 18, 22, 22, 25, 28, 30, 34. What is the median?
dq-0135.explanation: Correct: B. With seven scores in order, the fourth score, 25, is the median.

distractor_notes.A: 22 is the mode, not the median.
distractor_notes.C: 26 is the mean rounded to the nearest whole number.
distractor_notes.D: 28 is one of the scores but not the middle score.

dq-0136.question: Class X scores on a brain unit test are 70, 70, 70, 70, and 70. Class Y scores are 50, 60, 70, 80, and 90. Both classes have a mean of 70. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Class X has a larger range than Class Y.
Class Y has a lower mean than Class X.
Class Y has a larger range than Class X.
The two classes have the same range.
dq-0136.explanation: Correct: C. Class Y's scores range from 50 to 90, a range of 40, while Class X has a range of 0.

distractor_notes.A: Class X's scores are all identical, so its range is zero.
distractor_notes.B: Both classes have a mean of 70.
distractor_notes.D: Class Y's range is 40 and Class X's is 0.

dq-0137.question: After a stock market crash, Mr. Costa tells his friends, "I saw that coming all along," although he never made any prediction before the crash. Which of the following best describes his thinking?
dq-0137.explanation: Correct: D. Believing after an event that one knew it would happen is hindsight bias.

distractor_notes.A: Overconfidence is overestimating how much one knows or can do, not claiming to have predicted an event afterward.
distractor_notes.B: Confirmation bias is favoring information that supports existing beliefs.
distractor_notes.C: The availability heuristic judges likelihood by how easily examples come to mind.

dq-0138.question: Before a psychology test, students predict that they will each earn at least a 90. The average score turns out to be 72. Which of the following best explains the students' predictions?
dq-0138.explanation: Correct: A. Predicting much better performance than one actually achieves is overconfidence.

distractor_notes.B: Hindsight bias is a belief after the fact that an outcome was predictable.
distractor_notes.C: Confirmation bias is favoring information that agrees with existing beliefs.
distractor_notes.D: Skepticism is a willingness to question claims, which the students did not show.

dq-0139.question: Dr. Sato believes a new diet improves memory. She reads only the studies that support her belief and ignores studies that found no effect. Which of the following best describes her approach?
dq-0139.explanation: Correct: C. Searching only for evidence that agrees with a belief is confirmation bias.

distractor_notes.A: Hindsight bias is believing after the fact that one knew the outcome.
distractor_notes.B: Overconfidence is overestimating one's own knowledge or ability.
distractor_notes.D: Humility is acknowledging that one's ideas may be wrong.

dq-0140.question: Dr. Lopez reads a claim that a phone app doubles intelligence. She responds by asking to see the data and how the researchers collected it. Which of the following parts of the scientific attitude is Dr. Lopez showing?
dq-0140.explanation: Correct: B. Asking for evidence before accepting a claim shows skepticism.

distractor_notes.A: Curiosity is a desire to explore and ask questions.
distractor_notes.C: Humility is a willingness to admit one might be wrong.
distractor_notes.D: Overconfidence is not part of the scientific attitude.

dq-0141.question: After another lab fails to repeat his results, Dr. Banda publishes a correction and says that he may have been wrong. Which of the following parts of the scientific attitude is Dr. Banda showing?
dq-0141.explanation: Correct: A. Admitting that one's ideas may be wrong is humility.

distractor_notes.B: Skepticism is a willingness to question claims.
distractor_notes.C: Curiosity is a desire to explore and ask questions.
distractor_notes.D: Confirmation bias would lead him to defend his results.

dq-0142.question: A fair coin lands on heads six times in a row. Luis insists the coin must be rigged, even though runs like this happen by chance in many sequences of flips. Which of the following best describes his thinking?
dq-0142.explanation: Correct: D. People tend to see patterns in random events that chance alone can produce.

distractor_notes.A: Hindsight bias is believing after the fact that one knew the outcome.
distractor_notes.B: Overconfidence is overestimating one's knowledge or ability.
distractor_notes.C: Confirmation bias is favoring evidence that supports an existing belief.

dq-0143.question: Dr. Kim states that students who sleep eight hours will recall more words than students who sleep four hours. Which of the following terms best describes this statement?
dq-0143.explanation: Correct: B. A specific, testable prediction is a hypothesis.

distractor_notes.A: A theory is a broad explanation that organizes many observations.
distractor_notes.C: An operational definition states how a variable is measured.
distractor_notes.D: Replication is repeating a study.

dq-0144.question: After many observations, psychologists propose a set of principles that explains why people forget and predicts when forgetting will happen. Which of the following terms best describes these principles?
dq-0144.explanation: Correct: C. A broad explanation that organizes observations and generates predictions is a theory.

distractor_notes.A: A hypothesis is one specific testable prediction.
distractor_notes.B: An operational definition states how a variable is measured.
distractor_notes.D: Replication is repeating a study.

dq-0145.question: Dr. Obi defines aggression in her study as the number of times a child hits a doll in ten minutes. Which of the following best describes this definition?
dq-0145.explanation: Correct: D. Defining a variable by exactly how it will be measured is an operational definition.

distractor_notes.A: A theory is a broad explanation, not a measurement rule.
distractor_notes.B: Replication is repeating a study.
distractor_notes.C: A hypothesis is a prediction about results.

dq-0146.question: A research team in another country repeats a published experiment using the same procedures to see whether it gets the same results. Which of the following scientific practices is the team using?
dq-0146.explanation: Correct: A. Repeating a study to see whether results hold is replication.

distractor_notes.B: Peer review is expert evaluation before publication.
distractor_notes.C: An operational definition states how a variable is measured.
distractor_notes.D: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a repeat of a study.

dq-0147.question: Before a journal publishes a study, it sends the manuscript to independent experts, who judge the study's methods and conclusions. Which of the following best describes this process?
dq-0147.explanation: Correct: C. Having independent experts evaluate research before publication is peer review.

distractor_notes.A: Replication is repeating the study, not judging a manuscript.
distractor_notes.B: An operational definition states how a variable is measured.
distractor_notes.D: A hypothesis is a prediction.

dq-0148.question: A researcher wants to study stress. Which of the following is the best operational definition of stress for her study?
options: Stress is the general feeling of being overwhelmed by daily life.
Stress is a score on a 20-item worry and tension questionnaire.
Stress is whatever makes a person's life feel harder than usual.
Stress is the opposite of feeling relaxed and calm in life.
dq-0148.explanation: Correct: B. A measurable definition, such as a questionnaire score, lets others repeat the measurement.

distractor_notes.A: This describes the idea in general terms, not how it will be measured.
distractor_notes.C: This is vague and cannot be measured consistently.
distractor_notes.D: This defines stress by another vague term.

dq-0149.question: Which of the following is the best example of a testable hypothesis?
options: People who care about learning should sleep more each night.
Dreams always show what people secretly want but cannot admit.
Having a good memory is one of the most important abilities for success.
Students given a nap will recall more words than students given none.
dq-0149.explanation: Correct: D. A testable hypothesis predicts a specific, measurable result.

distractor_notes.A: This is an opinion, not a testable prediction.
distractor_notes.B: This cannot be checked with observable measures.
distractor_notes.C: This is too broad to test directly.

dq-0150.question: A researcher finds that her data do not support her hypothesis. According to the scientific method, which of the following is the best next step?
options: Revise the theory and test the new prediction.
Run the study again until the data support the hypothesis.
Report only the results that agree with the hypothesis.
Change the hypothesis and say it was predicted all along.
dq-0150.explanation: Correct: A. Science improves when theories are revised in light of evidence and then tested again.

distractor_notes.B: Repeating until results agree is biased.
distractor_notes.C: Leaving out results is dishonest.
distractor_notes.D: This is hindsight bias.

dq-0151.question: Dr. Reed explains why Mia studies so hard by pointing to the praise and good grades she receives after each study session. Which of the following psychological perspectives does this explanation best match?
dq-0151.explanation: Correct: C. Explaining behavior by rewards and consequences is the behavioral perspective.

distractor_notes.A: The humanistic perspective focuses on growth and free will.
distractor_notes.B: The evolutionary perspective focuses on survival and reproduction.
distractor_notes.D: The psychodynamic perspective focuses on unconscious conflicts.

dq-0152.question: Dr. Ortiz explains a student's test anxiety by how the student thinks about the test, including thoughts such as "I am going to fail." Which of the following psychological perspectives does this explanation best match?
dq-0152.explanation: Correct: D. Explaining behavior through thoughts and interpretations is the cognitive perspective.

distractor_notes.A: The behavioral perspective focuses on observable behavior and rewards.
distractor_notes.B: The biological perspective focuses on the brain and genes.
distractor_notes.C: The evolutionary perspective focuses on survival and reproduction.

dq-0153.question: Dr. Park studies how people strive to reach their full potential and how their sense of free will shapes their choices. Which of the following psychological perspectives does Dr. Park's work best match?
dq-0153.explanation: Correct: B. Focus on growth, potential, and free will is the humanistic perspective.

distractor_notes.A: The cognitive perspective focuses on mental processes.
distractor_notes.C: The psychodynamic perspective focuses on unconscious conflicts.
distractor_notes.D: The biological perspective focuses on the brain and genes.

dq-0154.question: Dr. Weiss explains an adult's persistent fear of close relationships by pointing to unconscious conflicts that began in early childhood. Which of the following psychological perspectives does this explanation best match?
dq-0154.explanation: Correct: A. Explaining behavior through unconscious conflicts from early life is the psychodynamic perspective.

distractor_notes.B: The behavioral perspective focuses on observable behavior.
distractor_notes.C: The humanistic perspective focuses on growth and free will.
distractor_notes.D: The evolutionary perspective focuses on survival and reproduction.

dq-0155.question: Dr. Tran explains one person's depression by pointing to differences in brain chemistry and in the person's family history. Which of the following psychological perspectives does this explanation best match?
dq-0155.explanation: Correct: B. Explaining behavior through the brain and heredity is the biological perspective.

distractor_notes.A: The sociocultural perspective focuses on culture and social context.
distractor_notes.C: The cognitive perspective focuses on mental processes.
distractor_notes.D: The humanistic perspective focuses on growth and free will.

dq-0156.question: Dr. Nakamura explains why people in two countries show respect to elders in different ways by pointing to each country's cultural norms and social setting. Which of the following psychological perspectives does this explanation best match?
dq-0156.explanation: Correct: C. Explaining behavior through culture and social context is the sociocultural perspective.

distractor_notes.A: The behavioral perspective focuses on rewards and consequences.
distractor_notes.B: The biological perspective focuses on the brain and genes.
distractor_notes.D: The evolutionary perspective focuses on survival and reproduction.
